dossier.public_summary: A 2.6 Earth-radius dip repeats every 13.5 days with a flat bottom, no odd-even difference, no secondary eclipse and consistent depths in 4 transits on an M dwarf. No nearby star within a TESS pixel can plausibly mimic it, and there is no sign of a large phase curve. The centroid is inconclusive at this brightness, so on-target confirmation remains uncertain, but a planet is the best current explanation.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma) opposes V-shaped grazing binary/eclipse despite b=0.6368 and duration ratio 1.404.
Planet-sized with undiluted depth 2048 ppm (rp_over_rstar 0.04526); well below stellar/threshold sizes.
No odd/even difference and secondary.snr 1.966 well below 5 (best_brightening_snr 2.717) with depth 359.9 ppm and depth_over_dip 0.1855, disfavoring EB at this or twice period 27 d.
No stars within 1 TESS pixel (21 arcsec) that could cause 2048 ppm dip with eclipse <=25%; closest that could needs 0.2003 at 75.6 arcsec, and contratio 0.000003366 is negligible.
4 transits with consistent depths (chi2 3.4915342840212964 dof 3, share_of_top_3 0.869) and refit.snr 9.639 with share 0.3716; signal not driven by few outliers, refit SNR above 7.
No large phase-curve swing (ratio_to_depth 0.06118, chi2 3.337 dof 9, variability_chi2_dof 0.3708); active M dwarf (teff 3482 VARIABLE) but dip remains transit-shaped, not spot-like.

No significant depth change between sectors (2438 vs 1753 ppm, chi2 2.039) and centroid verdict inconclusive with no sector showing clear difference image (centroid_all not_run) leaving no off-target evidence, though unable to fully localize without good S/N difference image.
